html:
The British invasions of the River Plate were two attempts by British forces to seize Buenos Aires and Montevideo, in 1806 and 1807. Both were defeated by local troops and townspeople.

In June 1806 a small British force took Buenos Aires with ease, as the Spanish viceroy fled. Weeks later, militias led by Santiago de Liniers retook the city. In 1807 a larger British army captured Montevideo and attacked Buenos Aires again, but the people fought from rooftops and streets, and the British surrendered.

The Spanish viceroy had failed, while creole militias had won. Liniers was made viceroy by popular choice, and the militia regiments became a political force. Their confidence led straight to the May Revolution of 1810 and the independence of Argentina.
sum: The British invasions of the River Plate were two attempts by British forces to seize Buenos Aires and Montevideo, in 1806 and 1807. Both were defeated by local troops and townspeople.
